Surah "Al-Muzzammil" (The Enshrouded One)

In the Name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

﴿O you who are wrapped up!﴾ That is, al-Mutazammil, the one who wraps himself in his garments, i.e., who covers himself with them, with the ta' assimilated into the zay. The Prophet ﷺ was sleeping at night, wrapped in his garments, so he was commanded to stand for prayer, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verses 2–3:

﴿Stand [in prayer] through the night, except for a little﴾ ﴿half of it﴾. "Half of it" is a substitution (badal) for "the night," and "except for a little" is an exception from His saying "half of it." Its implied sense is: "Stand half the night, except for a little of the half of the night."

﴿Or reduce from it﴾, from the half, with the waw vowelled with a ḍamma (أو انقص بضم الواو), by all readers except ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza,

﴿a little﴾, down to the third.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verses 2–3:

﴿Stand [in prayer] through the night, except for a little﴾ ﴿half of it﴾. "Half of it" is a substitution (badal) for "the night," and "except for a little" is an exception from His saying "half of it." Its implied sense is: "Stand half the night, except for a little of the half of the night."

﴿Or reduce from it﴾, from the half, with the waw vowelled with a ḍamma (أو انقص بضم الواو), by all readers except ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza,

﴿a little﴾, down to the third.

"Or add to it" (to the half), up to two-thirds. The intended meaning is a choice between two matters: he may stand for definitely less than half the night, or he may choose one of two options, either reducing from the half or adding to it. If you take "nisfahu" (half of it) as a substitute (badal) for "qalilan" (a little), he has the choice among three things: standing for exactly half the night, standing for less than half of it, or standing for more than half of it. He described the half as "little" in relation to the whole. Otherwise the word "qalil" applies to what is less than half. That is why we say: if someone acknowledges that so-and-so owes him a thousand dirhams "except a little," he is liable for more than half of the thousand.

"And recite the Qur'an [tarteel]" (measured, distinct recitation): clarify, make distinct, and articulate it. It comes from "al-thaghr al-murattal," meaning one with well-separated teeth (mufallaj al-asnan). It also comes from "kalam ratal," with the vowel on the second letter (ratal), meaning speech that is arranged in order (murattal), and "thaghr ratal" likewise, when the teeth are evenly set. Alternatively, it means: read with deliberation and calm, making each letter clearly distinct, observing the pauses (waqf) and giving the vowels their full length (ishba' al-harakat).

"Measured recitation [tartilan]": this is an emphasis on the obligation of the command to recite in this way, and that it is indispensable for the reciter.

Surely We shall send down upon you a weighty word.

﴿Surely We shall cast upon you﴾: We shall send down upon you.

﴿A weighty word﴾: that is, the Qur'an, because of what it contains of commands and prohibitions, which are burdensome and heavy obligations upon those who are held accountable; or [it is weighty] upon the hypocrites; or it is a speech that has weight and substance, not trivial and light.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 6:

﴿Indeed, the rising of the night﴾ — with the hamza, other than Warsh — meaning the standing in prayer at night. It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that it is a verbal noun from "nasha'a," meaning to rise up and stand, on the pattern "fa'ila," like "al-'afiyah" (well-being). Or it means the worship that arises at night, i.e., occurs, or the hours of the night, because they arise moment by moment. Zayn al-'Abidin (the Ornament of the Worshippers) used to pray between the two 'isha' prayers and would say: "This is the rising of the night" (hadhihi nashi'at al-layl).

﴿It is firmer in tread﴾ — "wid'an" (wi-ta'an) — read by Ibn 'Amir (al-Shami) and Abu 'Amr: meaning that in it the heart of the one standing in prayer conforms to his tongue. It is narrated from al-Hasan: "more conformity between the secret and the public, because the sight of creatures is cut off." Others read "wiT'an," meaning it is heavier upon the one praying than the prayer of the day, because it drives away sleep at its time. From his saying ﷺ: "O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Mudar" (ﷺ).

﴿And more upright in speech﴾ — and more firm in utterance, and more established in recitation, because of the calm of voices and the cessation of movements.

"Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation (sabhan tawilan)": (that is) movement and turning about in your affairs and preoccupations, so empty yourself at night for the worship of your Lord; or (it means) a long free time for your sleep and rest.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 8:

﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾, and persist in His remembrance by night and by day. The remembrance of Allah (dhikr Allah) encompasses glorification (tasbih), declaration of His oneness (tahlil), magnification (takbir), prayer (salah), recitation of the Qur'an (tilawat al-Qur'an), and the study of knowledge (dirasat al-'ilm),

﴿and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾: sever yourself toward His worship from everything else. And "al-tabattul" (exclusive devotion, detachment, the act of cutting oneself off) is the severance toward Allah (exalted is He), by hoping for good from Him alone, to the exclusion of others. It was also said: it is the renunciation of the world and what is in it, and the seeking of what is with Allah. (p-557) ﴿Complete devotion (tabtil)﴾: the difference in the verbal noun adds emphasis, meaning "Allah has cut you off, so devote yourself"; or it was used out of regard for the requirements of the rhyme (fawasil).

Lord of the East and the West. [Read as] with the nominative (raf'): meaning "He is the Lord," or as a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is: "there is no god but He." With the genitive (jarr), read by [the Qur'an readers of] Syria (Shami) and Kufa (Kufi) except Hafs, it is an apposition (badal) to "your Lord." It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that it is [a case of] oath (qasam), with the particle of oath elided, as in: "By Allah, I will surely do it," and its response (jawab) is: "there is no god but He," like his saying: "By Allah, there is no one in the house except Zayd."

﴿So take Him as a guardian (wakil)﴾: a protector (waliyy) and a trustee (kafil), for what He has promised you of victory. Or, once you know that He is the King of the East and the West, and that there is no god but He, then take Him as a sufficient one (kafi) for your affairs. The benefit of the fa' (so) is that you should not delay, after you have come to know, in entrusting your affairs to the One, the Subduer (al-Qahhar), since there is no excuse for you in waiting after acknowledgment.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 10:

﴿Be patient over what they say﴾, concerning Me (the claims about the consort and the offspring), and concerning you, (the claims) that you are "the sorcerer" and "the poet,"

﴿And forsake them with a gracious forsaking﴾: keep away from them in your heart, and oppose them while maintaining good conduct toward them and refraining from requiting them. It has also been said that it is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of fighting (naskh, abrogation).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 11:

﴿And leave Me﴾ means: leave them to Me, for I am sufficient for them,

﴿and the deniers﴾, the leaders of Quraysh, is in the accusative as an object "along with" (maf'ul ma'ahu), or it is a conjunction (ʿatf) with "leave Me", meaning: leave me and them,

﴿possessors of luxury﴾, of comfort and ease (al-tanaʿʿum). With a kasra (i.e. niʿmah as ni‘ma, "favour"), it means bestowal (al-inʿam); with a damma, it means joy (al-masarrah),

﴿and give them respite﴾, a granting of respite,

﴿a little﴾, until the day of Badr, or until the Day of Resurrection.

Verse 12: ﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles⁠—⁠﴾ for the disbelievers, in the Hereafter,

﴿shackles﴾: heavy fetters, the plural of "nikl" (a single heavy fetter),

﴿and a blazing Fire﴾: a Fire that burns intensely.

And food that chokes, and a painful punishment.

Food that sticks in the throat, so that it cannot be swallowed: that is, ḍarīʿ (a thorny, poisonous plant of the Hijaz) and zaqqūm (a bitter tree of Hell).

"A painful punishment" whose pain reaches the heart. It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse and fell unconscious (ṣaʿiqa). And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he was fasting one evening, and food was brought to him, but this verse came to his mind, and he said: "Take it away." It was placed before him the second night, and the verse came to him again, and he said: "Take it away." And likewise the third night. Then Thabit al-Banani and others were informed, so they came and kept at him until he drank a sip of sawiq (a drink of ground grain mixed with water).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 15:

﴿Indeed, We have sent to you﴾, O people of Makkah,

﴿a messenger﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿as a witness against you﴾, who will testify against you on the Day of Resurrection concerning your disbelief and your denial,

﴿just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾, meaning Musa (peace be upon him).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 16:

﴿But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger﴾. That is: that same Messenger, since when an indefinite noun (nakira) is repeated as a definite (ma'rifa), the second is the very same as the first.

﴿So We seized him with a heavy seizing﴾: severe and harsh. The reason Moses and Pharaoh were singled out is that their story was widely known among the people of Makkah, because they were neighbours of the Jews.

﴿فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا﴾ [Then how will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day?] Here ﴿يَوْمًا﴾ is the *maf'ul* (object, al-maf'ul bihi) of "تَتَّقُونَ" (*tattaqun*, "you guard yourselves"). That is: how will you guard against the punishment of such a day, if you disbelieve? Or it is a *zarf* (adverb of time), meaning: how will you have *taqwa* (God-consciousness, guarding oneself) on the Day of Resurrection, if you disbelieve in the world? Or it is *mansub* (in the accusative) by "كَفَرْتُمْ" (*kafartum*, "you disbelieve"), understood through *ta'wil* (interpretation) as "جَحَدْتُمْ" (*jahadtum*, "you deny"). That is: how will you guard yourselves against God and fear Him, if you deny the Day of Resurrection and the recompense? This is because *taqwa* of God is fear of His punishment.

﴿يَجْعَلُ الوِلْدانَ﴾ [that will make the children] is a *sifah* (qualifying clause, attributive) of "يَوْمًا" (*yawman*, "a day"), and the returning pronoun (al-'a'id) is omitted, meaning: "فِيهِ" (*fihi*, "in it").

﴿شِيبًا﴾ [grey-haired] is due to its terror and severity. This is when "it is said to Adam (peace be upon him): 'Stand up and send forth the group of the Fire from your offspring.'" *Shيبًا* is the plural of "أشْيَبُ" (*ashyab*, "grey-haired"). It was also said that it is a figurative expression (*tamthil*) for intensifying the terror, as is said of a severe matter: "يَوْمَ يَشِيبُ نَواصِي الأطْفالُ" ("a day when the foreheads of children turn grey").

﴿The sky will be split asunder by it﴾. This is also a description of the Day as severe. That is, the sky, despite its magnitude and its firm construction, will be split asunder by it, meaning it will be cleft. So what do you think of other creatures? The masculine form of the verb is used in accordance with interpreting "the sky" as "the roof," or as "the sky is a thing that is split asunder." His saying "by it" means by the Day of Resurrection, meaning that the sky will be split because of the severity and terror of that Day, just as a thing is split by that which splits it.

﴿His promise has always been fulfilled﴾. The verbal noun (al-maṣdar, the noun denoting the action) is annexed (muḍāf) to the object (al-mafʿūl), which is the Day, or to the subject (al-fāʿil), which is Allah, Exalted and Majestic, meaning His promise is to be fulfilled. The word "mafʿūlan" means "occurring" or "coming to pass."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 19:

﴿Indeed, this﴾, i.e. the verses that speak of warning (waʿid),

﴿is a reminder﴾, i.e. an admonition,

﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾. That is: whoever wills may take admonition from them and take a way to God through piety (taqwa) and fear (khashya).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 73, verse 20:

﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than﴾: "adna" means "aqall" (less). The word "adna" (nearer), which is the closer, is used metaphorically for "aqall" (less), because when the distance between two things is near, the space between them is small, and when it is far, that space is great.

﴿two-thirds of the night﴾, with the lam vowelled with a ḍamma (u), except in the reading of Hisham.

﴿and half of it, and a third of it﴾: both are in the accusative (naṣb), conjoined to "adna" (less). This is the reading of Makki and Kufi. Whoever reads them in the genitive (jarr) conjoins them to "thuluthay" (two-thirds).

﴿and a group﴾: conjoined to the pronoun in "taqumu" (you stand). It is permissible without emphasis (tawkid) because of the intervening separator.

﴿of those with you﴾: meaning, a group of your companions also stands for that amount [of time].

﴿And Allah measures the night and the day﴾: meaning, no one can measure the night and the day, and no one knows the measures of their hours except Allah alone. The placing of His name, exalted and majestic, as the subject (mubtada') upon which "yaqdiru" is predicated indicates that He alone is specialized in measuring.

Then they stood [in prayer] until their feet swelled, so this was revealed: ﴿He knows that you will not be able to keep count of it﴾: meaning, you will not be able to sustain standing for these measures except with strain and hardship, and in that there is difficulty.

﴿So He has turned to you [in mercy]﴾: meaning, He lightened [the burden] for you and removed from you the obligation of the night prayer.

﴿So recite﴾: in the prayer, and the imperative here is for obligation (wujub); or, outside of it, and the imperative is for recommendation (nadb).

﴿what is easy﴾: for you.

﴿of the Qur'an﴾: Abu Hanifa narrated from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Whoever recites one hundred verses in a night is not recorded among the heedless, and whoever recites two hundred verses is recorded among the devout (qanitin)." It was also said that by "the Qur'an" is meant "the prayer," because it is a part of its pillars; that is: pray what is easy for you, and it is not impossible from the night prayer. This [ruling] abrogates the first, and then this was abrogated by the five daily prayers. Then he explained the wisdom in the abrogation (naskh), which is the impossibility of standing [in prayer through the night] for the sick, the travellers and the fighters, so he said: ﴿He knows that there will be among you﴾: meaning, "that it" is a lightened form of "innahu" (indeed), and the sīn (s) is a substitute for its lightening and the deletion of its subject.

﴿sick﴾: so the night standing is hard for them.

﴿and others travelling through the land﴾: that is, journeying.

﴿seeking﴾: a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "yadribuna" (travelling).

﴿of Allah's bounty﴾: His provision, through trade, or the seeking of knowledge.

﴿and others fighting in the way of Allah﴾: He equated the one who strives (mujahid) with the one who earns a living, because earning lawful sustenance is a form of jihad. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Any man who brings something to Madina from the cities of the Muslims, patiently and seeking reward, and sells it at the price of its day, he is among the martyrs with Allah." Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: "Allah has not created a death that I would die after being killed in the way of Allah more beloved to me than dying between the two rods of a saddle, travelling through the land, seeking of Allah's bounty."

﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾: He repeated the command to ease, because of the intensity of their caution.

﴿And establish the prayer﴾: the obligatory one.

﴿And give zakat﴾: the obligatory one.

﴿And lend to Allah﴾: by means of the voluntary acts. "Qard" linguistically means "cutting off": the lender cuts off that amount from his wealth and gives it to another; likewise the one who gives charity cuts off that amount from his wealth and makes it for Allah, exalted. He attributed it to Himself only so that one would not bestow favour upon the poor person in what he gives him in charity, because the poor person is a helper to him in that act of devotion, so he has no favour over him; rather, the favour is for the poor person over him.

﴿a good loan﴾: from what is lawful, with sincerity.

﴿And whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it﴾: that is, its reward, and this is the response of the conditional.

﴿with Allah, it is better﴾: than what you leave behind and abandon. So the second object of "tajiduhu" is "khayran" (better), and "huwa" is a separating pronoun (fasl). It is permissible, even though it does not occur between two definites, because "af'al min" (more ... than) resembles a definite, through its refusal to take the definite article.

﴿and greater in reward﴾: and more abundant in recompense.

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾: for sins, and for shortcomings in good deeds.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾: He covers over the people of sin and shortcoming.

﴿Merciful﴾: He lightens [the burden] for the people of hardship and of success.
